files.note: Richter JP2 test file in openjpeg-data input/conformance (not a T.803 profile stream)
1080p RGB, 5-3 reversible but only ~1.6% of raw size (rate-truncated, so not lossless), 1 layer

known_deviations.codestream: OpenJPEG 2.5.3 (Debian's opj_decompress) aborts with 'munmap_chunk(): invalid pointer' on this stream: tile 0 has two extra zero-length tile-parts (Psot 14, TPsot 1 and 2, TNsot 0). With those two tile-parts removed OpenJPEG decodes it, bit-identical to our decode of the unmodified stream (every sample 0). We accept the empty tile-parts; OpenJPEG's failure is the reference's, not a decoder disagreement.

known_deviations.jp2: Malformed pclr: it declares 4-bit palette columns (Bi = 3) but stores 8-bit values (0xFF, 0xBF, ...). Our palette keeps the low Bi+1 bits of each entry (task 6.1, JPEG2000/Color.lean), OpenJPEG passes the byte through (and then writes values up to 255 in a PGX declared 4-bit). PDF rendering is unaffected: the image dictionary's /ColorSpace /Indexed overrides the JPX colour information, so a PDF reader uses the codestream index plane, which is bit-exact.

pdf_jpx.note: 12608 x 16806, 4 components (212 Mpx): skipped by scripts/diff-images.py (--max-mpx 40). Our decoder refuses it under Limits.default (workSamples 847,560,192 > maxWorkSamples 2^28), also at reduce 3. A >= 20 Mpx real-world benchmark candidate (Plan 8.4) once the limits allow it.

known_deviations.codestream: Odd image origin (XOsiz = YOsiz = 1) with 2x2 sub-sampled chroma, converted sYCC->RGB by OpenJPEG's heuristic. Our up-sampling replicates chroma on the reference grid (T.800 B.2; task 6.1 decision), OpenJPEG's sycc420_to_rgb aligns it differently for odd origins: 30 of 1024 pixels differ, all in row 0 and in column 0 (odd rows). Our decoded components are identical to those of jpx_subsampling-10 (the same data at origin 0), where ours and OpenJPEG agree exactly.
